fields.intervention: Implement active closed-loop thermal control on the extruder and nozzle to compensate for ambient temperature rises above 35C, specifically by dynamically adjusting nozzle temperature setpoints based on real-time ambient readings to maintain consistent viscosity.
fields.expected_effect: Maintains consistent filament viscosity and pressure at the nozzle, preventing the under-extrusion or thermal drift that causes layer skipping.

fields.mechanism: Two-level ANOVA experimental design used to isolate impacts of print speed, nozzle temperature, and layer height on print quality
fields.intervention: Apply a two-level ANOVA design to the 3D printer to statistically isolate the effect of ambient temperature on layer adhesion versus extruder temperature; specifically, measure the extruder and bed temperature stability while varying ambient conditions.
fields.expected_effect: The statistical analysis will identify if the layer skipping is due to insufficient thermal mass or temperature fluctuations that disrupt the bond between the polycarbonate layers, allowing for a targeted thermal control adjustment.
fields.falsification_test: Run the ANOVA test; if nozzle temperature variance is not the significant factor and layer skipping persists when the ambient temperature is controlled or when the extruder is stabilized at a higher setpoint, the hypothesis that ambient heat causes the skip via thermal instability is false.
